posts.title: BEACON Act of 2026
posts.label: 📋 Reported by committee
posts.note: Veterans' Affairs, as amended, H. Rept. 119-838
posts.summary: The bill would direct the Department of Veterans Affairs to award grants to organizations conducting research on treatments for traumatic brain injury, with a focus on rigorous clinical trials testing neurorehabilitation approaches.
posts.meta: Veterans' Affairs Committee · Rep. Jack Bergman (R-MI)
posts.whatsNext: Floor scheduling (leadership decides if and when it gets a vote)

posts.headline: Added to the congressional calendars
bodyLines: S. 5602: A bill to prohibit the use of Federal funds for the planning and construction of any structure or monument at Memorial Circle at Columbia Island/ Lady Bird Johnson Park in the District of Columbia.
S. 5603: A bill to prohibit the demolition of Presidential memorials.

posts.title: Kay Hagan Tick Reauthorization Act
posts.label: 📜✍️ Signed by Pres. Trump
posts.summary: The law extends funding through fiscal year 2030 for the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention to combat diseases spread by ticks and mosquitoes, including developing a national strategy, supporting regional centers of excellence, and helping state, local, and tribal health departments build their capacity to prevent and respond to these diseases.
posts.meta: Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions Committee · Sen. Susan Collins (R-ME)
posts.whatsNext: Takes effect (on enactment unless the text sets other dates)

posts.title: A resolution expressing the sense of the Senate that it values the active participation of the Republic of Kosovo as the state partner of the Iowa National Guard over the past 15 years.
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Agreed to (unanimous consent)
posts.summary: The resolution expresses the Senate's appreciation for Kosovo's partnership with the Iowa National Guard over the past 15 years.
posts.meta: Sen. Chuck Grassley (R-IA)

posts.title: A resolution expressing support for the designation of September 2026 as "Sickle Cell Disease Awareness Month" in order to educate communities across the United States about sickle cell disease and the need for research, early detection methods, effective treatments, and preventative care programs with respect to complications from sickle cell disease and conditions related to sickle cell disease.
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Agreed to (unanimous consent)
posts.summary: The resolution would designate September 2026 as "Sickle Cell Disease Awareness Month" to help educate Americans about sickle cell disease and promote awareness of the importance of research, early detection, effective treatments, and preventative care programs for managing the disease and related conditions.
posts.meta: Sen. Tim Scott (R-SC)

posts.title: A resolution expressing support for the designation of the week of October 24, 2026, to October 31, 2026, as "Bat Week".
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Agreed to (unanimous consent)
posts.summary: The resolution would express support for designating a specific week in late October 2026 as "Bat Week" to raise awareness about bats and their importance to the environment.
posts.meta: Sen. Peter Welch (D-VT)

posts.title: A resolution recognizing and supporting the goals and ideals of National Forensic Science Week.
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Agreed to (unanimous consent)
posts.summary: The resolution aims to recognize and support National Forensic Science Week, celebrating the importance of forensic science and the professionals who use scientific methods to solve crimes and support the justice system.
posts.meta: Sen. Mike Crapo (R-ID)

posts.title: A resolution supporting the goals and ideals of a National Move Over Law Day.
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Agreed to (unanimous consent)
posts.summary: The resolution seeks to establish and promote a National Move Over Law Day to raise awareness about laws requiring drivers to slow down and change lanes when approaching stopped emergency vehicles and other roadside workers.
posts.meta: Sen. Richard Blumenthal (D-CT)

posts.title: A resolution designating September 2026 as "School Bus Safety Month".
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Agreed to (unanimous consent)
posts.summary: The resolution would designate September 2026 as "School Bus Safety Month" to raise awareness about the importance of school bus safety for students and communities.
posts.meta: Sen. Deb Fischer (R-NE)

posts.title: A resolution designating November 7, 2026, as "National Bison Day".
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Agreed to (unanimous consent)
posts.summary: The resolution would designate November 7, 2026, as "National Bison Day" to recognize the historical and cultural significance of bison to the United States.
posts.meta: Sen. John Hoeven (R-ND)

posts.title: A resolution designating September 30, 2026, as "National Veterans Suicide Prevention Day".
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Agreed to (unanimous consent)
posts.summary: The resolution would designate September 30, 2026, as "National Veterans Suicide Prevention Day" to raise awareness about suicide prevention efforts among veterans and honor those affected by veteran suicide.
posts.meta: Sen. Thomas Tillis (R-NC)

posts.title: A resolution designating September 2026 as "National Childhood Cancer Awareness Month".
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Agreed to (unanimous consent)
posts.summary: The resolution would designate September 2026 as "National Childhood Cancer Awareness Month" to raise awareness about childhood cancer and highlight the importance of supporting children battling the disease and their families.
posts.meta: Sen. Tim Scott (R-SC)

posts.title: A resolution commending and congratulating Texas A&M University for 150 years of service to the State of Texas and the United States.
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Agreed to (unanimous consent)
posts.summary: The resolution would commend and congratulate Texas A&M University for 150 years of service to Texas and the United States.
posts.meta: Sen. John Cornyn (R-TX)

posts.title: Survivor Justice Tax Prevention Act
posts.label: 🗳️ Motion to proceed filed
posts.summary: The bill would allow survivors of sexual abuse to exclude settlement and lawsuit damages from their federal taxable income, even without documented physical injuries. It would shift the burden to the IRS to prove damages weren't related to sexual conduct if a settlement explicitly states they were, and would require the IRS to publicize this tax exclusion.
posts.meta: Ways and Means Committee · Rep. Lloyd Smucker (R-PA)
posts.whatsNext: The Senate votes on taking it up (the motion can be withdrawn)

posts.title: Survivor Justice Tax Prevention Act
posts.label: ⏱️ Cloture motion filed
posts.summary: The bill would allow survivors of sexual abuse to exclude settlement and lawsuit damages from their federal taxable income, even without documented physical injuries. It would shift the burden to the IRS to prove damages weren't related to sexual conduct if a settlement explicitly states they were, and would require the IRS to publicize this tax exclusion.
posts.meta: Ways and Means Committee · Rep. Lloyd Smucker (R-PA)
posts.whatsNext: Cloture vote expected on the second session day (60 votes to advance)

posts.title: Stop Insider Trading Act
posts.label: ⏱️ Cloture not invoked (on taking up the bill) (53-47)
posts.summary: The bill would prohibit members of Congress and their spouses and dependent children from buying stocks in publicly traded companies. It would also require them to publicly announce their intention to sell such stocks at least a week in advance, with some exemptions for certain types of investments and employment-related transactions. Violations would result in fees and mandatory sale requirements.
posts.meta: House Administration · Rep. Bryan Steil (R-WI)
posts.whatsNext: Senate has not taken up the bill (60 votes not reached; a new vote can be sought)

posts.title: Ratepayer Protection Act
posts.label: 🗳️ Motion to proceed filed
posts.summary: The bill would amend federal utility regulation law to establish a standard allowing electric utilities to recover the full costs of infrastructure upgrades made specifically to serve large industrial or commercial customers. It aims to clarify how utilities can recoup expenses for these targeted system improvements from the businesses that directly benefit from them.
posts.meta: Energy and Commerce Committee · Rep. Gabe Evans (R-CO)
posts.whatsNext: The Senate votes on taking it up (the motion can be withdrawn)

posts.title: Ratepayer Protection Act
posts.label: ⏱️ Cloture not invoked (on taking up the bill) (57-43)
posts.summary: The bill would amend federal utility regulation law to establish a standard allowing electric utilities to recover the full costs of infrastructure upgrades made specifically to serve large industrial or commercial customers. It aims to clarify how utilities can recoup expenses for these targeted system improvements from the businesses that directly benefit from them.
posts.meta: Energy and Commerce Committee · Rep. Gabe Evans (R-CO)
posts.whatsNext: Senate has not taken up the bill (60 votes not reached; a new vote can be sought)

posts.title: To require the Secretary of Agriculture to convey the Pleasant Valley Ranger District Administrative Site to Gila County, Arizona.
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed Senate (unanimous consent)
posts.summary: The bill would require the federal government to transfer approximately 232.9 acres of National Forest land in Arizona to Gila County, provided the county commits to using the property to serve and support veterans. If the county stops using the land for that purpose, ownership would revert back to the federal government, and the county would bear all costs associated with the transfer, including surveys and environmental assessments.
posts.meta: Energy and Natural Resources Committee, Natural Resources Committee · Rep. Elijah Crane (R-AZ)

posts.title: End Tax Penalties on American Hostages Act
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed Senate (unanimous consent)
posts.summary: The bill would extend federal tax filing and payment deadlines for Americans who are unlawfully detained or held hostage abroad, as well as their spouses, and would allow the IRS to refund any late fees, interest, and penalties they were charged during their detention. It would require the State Department and Department of Justice to provide the IRS with annual lists of qualifying individuals, and would establish a program allowing affected people to claim refunds for penalties assessed since 2021.
posts.meta: Finance Committee, Ways and Means Committee · Rep. Claudia Tenney (R-NY)

posts.title: Indian Health Service Emergency Claims Parity Act
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed Senate (unanimous consent)
posts.summary: The bill would extend the deadline for notifying the Indian Health Service's payment program about emergency medical care received at non-IHS facilities from 72 hours to 15 days, giving patients and providers more time to report these claims. The extended timeline would not apply to elderly or disabled beneficiaries, who would continue to have 30 days to notify the program.
posts.meta: Indian Affairs Committee · Sen. Mike Rounds (R-SD)
posts.whatsNext: To the House (if and when it takes it up)

posts.title: Quinault Indian Nation Land Transfer Act
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed Senate with amendment (unanimous consent)
posts.summary: The bill would transfer approximately 72 acres of federal forest land in Washington to the Department of the Interior, which would then hold it in trust for the Quinault Indian Nation as part of the tribe's reservation. The measure prohibits gambling on the transferred land and requires the department to disclose any hazardous substances on the property, though it would not require cleanup of those substances.
posts.meta: Indian Affairs Committee · Sen. Maria Cantwell (D-WA)
posts.whatsNext: To the House (if and when it takes it up)

posts.title: Floodplain Enhancement and Recovery Act
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed Senate (unanimous consent)
posts.summary: The bill would amend federal flood insurance law to support ecosystem restoration projects, with the aim of enhancing natural areas and potentially reducing flood risks. It seeks to integrate environmental recovery efforts with the existing framework governing homeowner flood insurance.
posts.meta: Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs Committee · Sen. Patty Murray (D-WA)
posts.whatsNext: To the House (if and when it takes it up)

posts.title: Wyoming Education Trust Modernization Act
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed Senate (unanimous consent)
posts.summary: The bill would modify how Wyoming manages its permanent school fund, which was established from federal land grants when the state was created. It would allow Wyoming to use investment earnings from the fund to support public schools, not just interest payments, giving the state greater flexibility in funding education.
posts.meta: Energy and Natural Resources Committee · Sen. Cynthia Lummis (R-WY)
posts.whatsNext: To the House (if and when it takes it up)

posts.title: Snow Water Supply Forecasting Program Reauthorization Act of 2026
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed Senate with amendment (unanimous consent)
posts.summary: The bill would reauthorize the Snow Water Supply Forecasting Program, which helps predict water availability from snowpack for planning and management purposes. It aims to extend the program's authorization to continue supporting water resource forecasting efforts across affected regions.
posts.meta: Energy and Natural Resources Committee · Sen. John Hickenlooper (D-CO)
posts.whatsNext: To the House (if and when it takes it up)

posts.title: National Park System Long-Term Lease Investment Act
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed Senate with amendment (unanimous consent)
posts.summary: The bill would allow the Secretary of the Interior to extend certain leases within National Park System units without requiring those leases to go through a competitive bidding process.
posts.meta: Energy and Natural Resources Committee · Sen. Thomas Tillis (R-NC)
posts.whatsNext: To the House (if and when it takes it up)

posts.title: Crystal Reservoir Conveyance Act
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed Senate with amendment (unanimous consent)
posts.summary: The bill would direct the U.S. Department of Agriculture to transfer ownership of certain Forest Service land and a reservoir to the City of Ouray, Colorado.
posts.meta: Energy and Natural Resources Committee · Sen. Michael Bennet (D-CO)
posts.whatsNext: To the House (if and when it takes it up)

posts.title: Health Care Cybersecurity and Resiliency Act of 2026
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed Senate with amendment (unanimous consent)
posts.summary: The bill would require private health care organizations to adopt minimum cybersecurity protections like multifactor authentication and would direct federal health agencies to provide training, guidance, and resources to strengthen cybersecurity across the health care sector. It would also require HHS and the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency to coordinate their efforts to prevent and respond to cyberattacks, and would mandate that health care providers notify patients about the number of people affected when their personal health information is breached.
posts.meta: Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions Committee · Sen. Bill Cassidy (R-LA)
posts.whatsNext: To the House (if and when it takes it up)

posts.title: Safe Access to Cash Act of 2026
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed Senate with amendment (voice vote)
posts.summary: The bill would create new federal crimes for tampering with, damaging, or interfering with automated teller machines (ATMs), whether located at banks or elsewhere, and would establish penalties for such violations.
posts.meta: Judiciary Committee · Sen. Ted Cruz (R-TX)
posts.whatsNext: To the House (if and when it takes it up)

posts.title: MORE American Fuel Act of 2026
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed Senate with amendment (unanimous consent)
posts.summary: The bill would amend federal atomic energy law to treat uranium enrichment facilities the same way the government treats other nuclear fuel processing facilities when it comes to licensing and regulation. This change aims to streamline the oversight process for uranium enrichment operations under existing atomic energy statutes.
posts.meta: Environment and Public Works Committee · Sen. Mark Kelly (D-AZ)
posts.whatsNext: To the House (if and when it takes it up)

posts.title: A resolution supporting the designation of October 2026 as "Substance Use & Misuse Prevention Month" to raise awareness of substance use and misuse in the United States.
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Agreed to (unanimous consent)
posts.summary: The resolution would designate October 2026 as "Substance Use & Misuse Prevention Month" to increase public awareness about substance use and misuse across the United States.
posts.meta: Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions Committee · Sen. Pete Ricketts (R-NE)

posts.title: A resolution designating October 8, 2026, as "National Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Day".
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Agreed to (unanimous consent)
posts.summary: The resolution would designate October 8, 2026, as "National Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Day" to recognize and raise awareness about hydrogen and fuel cell technologies and their potential role in addressing energy and environmental challenges.
posts.meta: Sen. Richard Blumenthal (D-CT)

posts.title: A resolution recognizing the seriousness of polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) and expressing support for the designation of September 2026 as "PCOS Awareness Month".
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Agreed to (unanimous consent)
posts.summary: The resolution seeks to recognize polycystic ovary syndrome as a serious health condition and express support for designating September 2026 as "PCOS Awareness Month" to increase public understanding of this common reproductive health disorder.
posts.meta: Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-MA)

posts.title: A resolution to honor the Americans killed by Hamas terrorists and their affiliates on and after October 7, 2023, to reaffirm the commitment of the United States to seek legal justice on behalf of their families, and for other purposes.
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Agreed to (unanimous consent)
posts.summary: The resolution would honor Americans killed by Hamas terrorists and their affiliates, reaffirm the U.S. commitment to pursuing legal justice for the victims and their families, and express solidarity with those affected by these attacks.
posts.meta: Sen. Rick Scott (R-FL)

posts.title: Choices for Increased Mobility Act of 2026
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed Senate (voice vote)
posts.summary: The bill would require Medicare to create specific billing codes for ultralightweight manual wheelchairs, including at least one code for wheelchairs made with titanium or carbon fiber and one for those without these materials. It would allow suppliers to bill Medicare patients for the difference between Medicare's payment and the actual cost of the wheelchair.
posts.meta: Finance Committee, Ways and Means Committee, Energy and Commerce Committee · Rep. John Joyce (R-PA)

posts.title: Clergy Act
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed Senate (unanimous consent)
posts.summary: The bill would create a two-year period during which members of the clergy and Christian Science practitioners could revoke their previous exemption from Social Security and Medicare taxes, allowing them to gain retirement benefits they would otherwise forgo. It would also require the IRS to develop a plan to inform eligible individuals about this opportunity to change their status.
posts.meta: Finance Committee, Ways and Means Committee · Rep. Vince Fong (R-CA)

posts.title: Pit River Land Transfer Act of 2026
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed Senate with amendment (unanimous consent)
posts.summary: The bill would transfer approximately 603.94 acres of federal and tribal land in California into trust status for the Pit River Tribe, making it part of the tribe's reservation. The measure would prohibit gambling operations on the transferred land.
posts.meta: Indian Affairs Committee, Natural Resources Committee · Rep. Doug LaMalfa (R-CA)
posts.whatsNext: Back to the House (amendments must match exactly)

posts.title: Enhancing Detection of Human Trafficking Act
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed Senate (unanimous consent)
posts.summary: The bill would require the Department of Labor to train its employees on how to recognize signs of human trafficking and assist law enforcement in preventing it. The training would be tailored to employees based on their job duties and local conditions, covering current detection methods and how to refer suspected cases to the Department of Justice and other authorities.
posts.meta: Education and Workforce Committee · Rep. Tim Walberg (R-MI)

posts.title: Skills-Based Federal Contracting Act of 2025
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed Senate (unanimous consent)
posts.summary: The bill would prevent federal agencies from requiring job applicants on government contracts to have minimum educational credentials—such as a college degree—unless contracting officers can justify why education is truly necessary for the position. It also directs the federal government to issue guidance encouraging agencies to consider work experience and skills as alternatives to formal education requirements when hiring for these contracts.
posts.meta: Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee, Oversight and Government Reform Committee · Rep. Nancy Mace (R-SC)

posts.title: TAS Act
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed Senate with amendment (unanimous consent)
posts.summary: The bill would expand the U.S. Tax Court's authority to issue subpoenas for documents and evidence outside of scheduled hearings, allow the court to extend filing deadlines when it's fair to do so, and authorize special trial judges to impose fines and jail time for contempt of court. It would also expand when special trial judges can be assigned to cases and establish rules requiring judges to recuse themselves in certain situations.
posts.meta: Finance Committee, Ways and Means Committee · Rep. Nathaniel Moran (R-TX)
posts.whatsNext: Back to the House (amendments must match exactly)

posts.title: Chiricahua National Park Act
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed Senate (unanimous consent)
posts.summary: The bill would redesignate Chiricahua National Monument in Arizona as a national park. It would require the National Park Service to protect traditional cultural and religious sites within the park and allow Native American tribes to access these areas for customary uses, with the ability to request temporary closures of specific park areas to accommodate tribal ceremonies and activities.
posts.meta: Energy and Natural Resources Committee, Natural Resources Committee · Rep. Juan Ciscomani (R-AZ)

posts.title: Mystic Alerts Act
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed Senate (unanimous consent)
posts.summary: The bill would allow wireless emergency alerts to be transmitted to mobile devices via satellite in addition to current terrestrial networks. It would require participating mobile service providers to notify the FCC about whether they will offer satellite alerts, establish technical standards for such alerts, and allow both providers and consumers to opt out of satellite alert transmission.
posts.meta: Commerce, Science, and Transportation Committee, Energy and Commerce Committee · Rep. August Pfluger (R-TX)

posts.title: License to Drill Act
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed Senate (unanimous consent)
posts.summary: The bill would extend the federal government's authority to collect fees from oil and gas companies when they apply for drilling permits on public lands. Currently set to expire in 2026, these fees—which support the permit review process—would continue through 2037.
posts.meta: Energy and Natural Resources Committee, Natural Resources Committee · Rep. Mike Kennedy (R-UT)

posts.title: Criminal History Access Act of 2026
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed Senate (unanimous consent)
posts.summary: The bill would allow state and territorial agencies that set standards and certifications for law enforcement officers to access criminal history records maintained by the FBI. This aims to help these agencies better screen and evaluate police officers during hiring, training, and retention processes.
posts.meta: Judiciary Committee · Rep. Derek Schmidt (R-KS)
